Question_text: Simon wants to motivate his production workers to work harder. Identify two methods he could use to motivate production workers at Everyday Suits. Explain why these methods would be effective.
Sub_topic: Reasons people work, meaning of motivation
Financial rewards: wage, salary, bonus, commission, profit sharing
Non-financial: job enrichment, rotation, teamworking, training, promotion
Recommend, justify motivation methods

Question_text: Appendix 2 shows the proposed new organisation chart for Everyday Suits. Simon will not be able to do all the work himself if the business grows bigger. Choose four departments that Simon could create and justify why each department could be important to the success of the business.
Sub_topic: Draw, interpret organisational charts
Hierarchical structures: levels, span of control, chain of command, chain of tall/short
Functions: planning, organising, coordinating, commanding, controlling

Question_text: Refer to Appendix 3. Identify and explain two ways Simon could increase the added value of his current business.
Sub_topic: Concept of adding value, increasing added value

Question_text: To expand the business Simon may need new machinery. To finance this, he is considering using an overdraft or leasing the equipment or selling more shares. Consider these three options for raising finance and recommend which one he should choose. Justify your choice.
Sub_topic: Reasons for finance: start-up, expansion, working capital
Short-term/long-term sources: overdraft, debt, equity
Factors in choice: size, legal form, amount, time, loans
Recommend, justify source(s)

Question_text: As Everyday Suits expands it will need to employ new managers. Identify and explain four parts of an induction training programme for new managers.
Topic: 2.3 Recruitment, selection and training of employees
Sub_topic: Importance of training to business, employees
Benefits, limitations: induction, on-the-job, off-the-job training

Question_text: Simon thinks that Option 1 would require a different marketing mix to Option 2. In what ways do you think each of the elements of the marketing mix will be different for Option 1 and Option 2? Justify your answer.
Sub_topic: Limitations, benefits of new products
Pricing methods: cost plus, competitive, penetration, skimming, promotional
Advantages, disadvantages of channels: wholesalers, retailers, direct
Aims of promotion
Forms: advertising, sales promotion, influence on sales
Importance of marketing mix elements in decisions
Recommend, justify strategy

Question_text: As Everyday Suits expands it could gain from economies of scale. Identify and explain two examples of economies of scale the business might benefit from as it expands.
Topic: 4.2 Costs, scale of production and break-even analysis
Sub_topic: Concept of economies of scale, examples: purchasing, marketing, financial, managerial, technical

Question_text: Using the information in Appendix 1, do you think Simon should be satisfied with the financial position of the business? Justify your answer using appropriate ratios.
Sub_topic: Concept, importance of profitability
Concept, importance of liquidity
Interpret performance: calculate, analyse ratios
Ratios: gross profit margin, profit margin, return on capital employed, current ratio, acid test ratio
Use for decisions: lend, invest

Question_text: Everyday Suits currently uses batch production. However, if Simon chooses Option 1 job production will be used or if he follows Option 2 flow production will be used. Explain the main features of job production for Option 1 and the main features of flow production for Option 2.
Sub_topic: Features, benefits, limitations: job, batch, flow production
Recommend, justify production method

Question_text: Simon will need to use new machinery in the production of suits if he chooses Option 2. Do you think that the production workers at Everyday Suits would think the use of new machinery was a good idea or not? Justify your answer.
Sub_topic: Reasons people work, meaning of motivation
Benefits: productivity, reduced absenteeism, turnover
Situations for downsizing: automation, reduced demand
Changes from technology: computers in design, manufacturing
Benefits, limitations: induction, on-the-job, off-the-job training
